docs.title: Pydantic GSheets
docs.text: Pydantic GSheets binds Google Sheets data to typed Pydantic models. This documentation covers the public classes and functions available to build applications on top of the library.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Authentication
  • Worksheet interaction
  • Smartchips

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The library accepts any google.auth.credentials.Credentials object directly. Four factory helpers cover every real-world auth pattern. Pass the resulting credentials to build_sheets_service() / build_drive_service() to get API clients.

docs.title: credentials_from_service_account_file(key_file, *, scopes=DEFAULT_SCOPES)
docs.text:
Load a service account from a JSON key file downloaded from Google Cloud Console. Best for server-side / CI environments.

from pydantic_gsheets import credentials_from_service_account_file, build_sheets_service

creds = credentials_from_service_account_file("service_account.json")
service = build_sheets_service(creds)

docs.title: credentials_from_service_account_info(info, *, scopes=DEFAULT_SCOPES)
docs.text:
Same as above but accepts an already-parsed dict (e.g. loaded from a secret manager), avoiding a file on disk.

import json
info = json.loads(os.environ["SA_JSON"])
creds = credentials_from_service_account_info(info)

docs.title: credentials_from_adc(*, scopes=DEFAULT_SCOPES, quota_project_id=None)
docs.text:
Application Default Credentials — automatically detects the environment (GCE, Cloud Run, GKE, local gcloud auth application-default login). Ideal for code that runs both locally and on GCP without config changes.

from pydantic_gsheets import credentials_from_adc, build_sheets_service

creds = credentials_from_adc()
service = build_sheets_service(creds)

docs.title: credentials_from_user_oauth(client_secrets_file, *, token_cache_file="token.json", scopes=DEFAULT_SCOPES, local_server_port=0)
docs.text:
Interactive browser-based OAuth2 flow for end-user sign-in. Opens a browser on first use; subsequent runs load the cached token automatically.

from pydantic_gsheets import credentials_from_user_oauth, build_sheets_service

creds = credentials_from_user_oauth("client_secrets.json")
service = build_sheets_service(creds)
Parameter Type Description client_secrets_file str Path to the OAuth client JSON from Google Cloud Console. token_cache_file str Where to persist the refreshable token. Default "token.json". scopes Sequence[str] OAuth scopes to request. Defaults to DEFAULT_SCOPES. local_server_port int Port for the local callback server. 0 picks a free port.

docs.title: build_sheets_service(credentials)
docs.text: Returns an authenticated googleapiclient.discovery.Resource for Sheets v4.

docs.title: build_drive_service(credentials)
docs.text: Returns an authenticated googleapiclient.discovery.Resource for Drive v3. Only needed if you use Drive-specific features (file chips, etc.).

docs.title: Scope Constants
docs.text:
from pydantic_gsheets import SHEETS_RW, SHEETS_RO, DRIVE_FULL, DRIVE_FILE
Constant Scope Description SHEETS_RW …/auth/spreadsheets Full Sheets read/write SHEETS_RO …/auth/spreadsheets.readonly Sheets read-only DRIVE_FULL …/auth/drive Full Drive access DRIVE_FILE …/auth/drive.file Only files created by this app

DEFAULT_SCOPES = (SHEETS_RW, DRIVE_FILE) — least privilege for typical use.

docs.title: SheetsClient
docs.text:
SheetsClient wraps a raw Resource and adds automatic retry and rate limiting to every API call.

from pydantic_gsheets import SheetsClient, RetryConfig

client = SheetsClient(
    service,
    retry_config=RetryConfig(max_attempts=5),
)
ws = GoogleWorkSheet(model=MyRow, service=client, ...)

GoogleWorkSheet also accepts a raw Resource directly (it wraps it in a SheetsClient automatically), but passing a SheetsClient lets you tune retry behaviour.

docs.title: Deprecated API
docs.text: AuthConfig, AuthMethod, get_sheets_service(), and get_drive_service() from pydantic_gsheets.auth.factory still work but emit a DeprecationWarning and will be removed in v3. Migrate to the factory functions above.

docs.title: Smart Chips
docs.text: Smart chips are rich, interactive cells in Google Sheets that can link to Drive files, people, calendar events, YouTube videos, and places. pydantic-gsheets parses chips on read and emits them on write where supported.

docs.title: Supported Types
docs.text:
Class Readable Writable Description fileSmartChip / FileSmartChip ✅ ✅ Google Drive file link peopleSmartChip / PeopleSmartChip ✅ ✅ Person / email chip eventSmartChip / EventSmartChip ✅ ❌ Calendar event (read-only) placeSmartChip / PlaceSmartChip ✅ ❌ Location (read-only) youtubeSmartChip / YouTubeSmartChip ✅ ❌ YouTube video (read-only) richLinkProperties / RichLinkProperties ✅ ✅ Generic rich link

Attempting to write a read-only chip type raises NotImplementedError.

docs.title: Writing Smart Chips
docs.text: Write access to Drive file chips requires the drive.file, drive.readonly, or drive OAuth scope. These are included in DEFAULT_SCOPES.

docs.title: Declaring Smart Chip Fields
docs.text:
Use GS_SMARTCHIP (or its alias GSSmartChip) as an annotation marker on a field typed as SmartChips:

from pydantic_gsheets import SheetRow, GSIndex, GSRequired, GS_SMARTCHIP
from pydantic_gsheets.types.smart_chips import SmartChips, peopleSmartChip, fileSmartChip
from typing import Annotated

class MyRow(SheetRow):
    owner_and_file: Annotated[
        SmartChips,
        GS_SMARTCHIP("@ owns @", smartchips=[peopleSmartChip, fileSmartChip]),
        GSIndex(0),
        GSRequired(),
    ]

The format_text string uses @ as a placeholder for each chip in order. Use \@ for a literal @ character.

docs.title: Reading Smart Chips
docs.text:
When a row is read, the field will be a SmartChips instance:

for row in ws.rows():
    chips = row.owner_and_file
    print(chips.display_text)       # raw cell text
    print(chips.chipRuns[0].email)  # peopleSmartChip
    print(chips.chipRuns[1].uri)    # fileSmartChip

docs.title: Writing Smart Chips
docs.text:
Assign a SmartChips instance and call save():

from pydantic_gsheets.types.smart_chips import SmartChips, peopleSmartChip, fileSmartChip

row.owner_and_file = SmartChips(
    format_text="@ owns @",
    chipRuns=[
        peopleSmartChip(email="alice@example.com"),
        fileSmartChip(uri="https://drive.google.com/file/d/FILE_ID"),
    ],
)
row.save()

docs.title: smartChip (base)
docs.text: Abstract base for all chip types. Defines __fieldName__ class variable and _to_dict() method.

docs.title: richLinkProperties / RichLinkProperties
docs.text: • uri: str — the link URI.

docs.title: personProperties
docs.text:
• email: str
  • display_format: displayFormat — DEFAULT, LAST_NAME_COMMA_FIRST_NAME, or EMAIL.

docs.title: peopleSmartChip / PeopleSmartChip
docs.text: Subclass of personProperties.

docs.title: fileSmartChip / FileSmartChip
docs.text: Subclass of richLinkProperties. The only writable rich-link chip type.

docs.title: eventSmartChip, placeSmartChip, youtubeSmartChip
docs.text: Read-only subclasses of richLinkProperties. _to_dict() raises NotImplementedError.

docs.title: SmartChips (also smartChips)
docs.text: Container returned when reading a smart chip field. - display_text: str | None — raw cell text. - format_text: str | None — the @-pattern format string. - chipRuns: list[smartChip] — parsed chip objects in order.

docs.title: GS_SMARTCHIP / GSSmartChip
docs.text: Annotation marker dataclass. - format_text: str — @-pattern string. Default "@". - smartchips: list[type[smartChip]] — chip types in the same order as @ tokens.

docs.title: SmartChipConfig (also smartchipConf)
docs.text: Internal Pydantic model storing parsed chip config per field. Not part of the public annotation API.

docs.title: Worksheet Interaction
docs.text: API for representing Google Sheet tabs as typed Pydantic models and reading/writing row data.

docs.title: Annotation Markers
docs.text: Markers are placed inside Annotated[...] on SheetRow field definitions.

docs.title: GSIndex(index: int)
docs.text:
Zero-based column position relative to start_column. If omitted, columns are assigned positions in definition order.

name: Annotated[str, GSIndex(0)]
age:  Annotated[int, GSIndex(2)]   # column B is skipped

docs.title: GSRequired(message="")
docs.text: Field must be non-empty on read and write. Raises RequiredValueError when violated. Must be instantiated — GSRequired() not GSRequired.

docs.title: GSParse(func)
docs.text: Apply func(raw_string) to the cell value before Pydantic validation. Useful for custom string-to-type conversions.

docs.title: GSFormat(number_format_type, pattern=None)
docs.text: Desired Google Sheets number format for the column (e.g. "DATE_TIME", "CURRENCY"). Applied via GoogleWorkSheet.apply_formats_for_model().

docs.title: GSReadonly()
docs.text: Field is never written back to the sheet. Drive link chips and read-only chip types are marked readonly automatically.

docs.title: GSTreatDashAsEmpty()
docs.text: Opt-in: treat the literal string "-" as an empty/None value for this field. Without this marker, "-" passes through unchanged.

docs.title: GS_SMARTCHIP(format_text="@", smartchips=[...])
docs.text: Declares a field as containing smart chips. See Smart Chips.

docs.title: RequiredValueError(field_name, row_number)
docs.text: Raised when a GSRequired field is empty. Carries .field_name and .row_number attributes.

docs.title: ParseError(field_name, col_index, cause)
docs.text: Raised when a GSParse callable throws. Carries .field_name, .col_index, and .__cause__.

docs.title: UnboundRowError
docs.text: Raised when save() or reload() is called on a row not yet bound to a worksheet.

docs.title: SchemaError
docs.text: Raised at model definition time for invalid annotations (duplicate GSIndex, bare GSRequired class without (), etc.).

docs.title: RateLimitError / TransientAPIError
docs.text: Raised after all retry attempts are exhausted (429 and 5xx respectively).

docs.title: RequiredValueSkippedWarning
docs.text: UserWarning emitted when a row is skipped because a required field is empty (instead of silently discarding it).

docs.title: SheetRow
docs.text:
Base class for typed rows. Subclass and annotate fields with Annotated.

from pydantic_gsheets import SheetRow, GSIndex, GSRequired, GSFormat
from typing import Annotated
from datetime import datetime

class MyRow(SheetRow):
    username: Annotated[str,      GSIndex(0), GSRequired()]
    age:      Annotated[int,      GSIndex(1)]
    joined:   Annotated[datetime, GSIndex(2), GSFormat("DATE_TIME", "dd-MM-yyyy HH:mm")]

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• row_number — absolute 1-based row number in the sheet (raises UnboundRowError if not bound).
  • worksheet — the GoogleWorkSheet the row is bound to.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
• save() — write the current instance back to its bound row.
  • reload() — refresh the instance from the sheet.

docs.title: GoogleWorkSheet[T]
docs.text: Generic wrapper around a single worksheet tab.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
GoogleWorkSheet(
    model,
    service,          # SheetsClient or raw Resource (deprecated)
    spreadsheet_id,
    sheet_name,
    *,
    start_row=2,
    start_column=0,
    validate_access=True,
)
Parameter Type Description model Type[T] The SheetRow subclass for this sheet. service SheetsClient or Resource Authenticated API client. spreadsheet_id str Google Sheets spreadsheet ID. sheet_name str Name of the worksheet tab. start_row int First data row (1-based). Default 2 (assumes a header row). start_column int Column offset (0 = column A). validate_access bool Verify read/write permissions on init. Default True.

docs.title: GoogleWorkSheet.create_sheet(model, service, spreadsheet_id, sheet_name, *, add_column_headers=True, skip_if_exists=True, start_row=2, start_column=0)
docs.text: Create a new sheet tab and return a bound GoogleWorkSheet. If the tab already exists and skip_if_exists=True, opens the existing tab instead.

docs.title: rows(*, refresh=False, skip_rows_missing_required=True, page_size=None)
docs.text: Generator yielding all data rows as typed instances. Results are cached; pass refresh=True to re-read from the sheet. Use page_size to read large sheets in chunks (reduces memory usage).

docs.title: get(row_number, *, use_cache=True, refresh=False, skip_rows_missing_required=True) → T | None
docs.text: Fetch a single row by absolute 1-based row number. Returns None if a required field is empty and skip_rows_missing_required=True.

docs.title: saveRow(inst) / saveRows(rows)
docs.text: Save one or multiple already-bound row instances.

docs.title: append_row(instance) → T
docs.text:
Append an unbound SheetRow instance as a new row at the end of data. Binds the instance to its new row number and returns it.

new_row = MyRow(username="alice", age=30, joined=datetime.now())
ws.append_row(new_row)
print(new_row.row_number)  # e.g. 5

docs.title: append_rows(instances) → list[T]
docs.text: Append multiple unbound rows in a single batchUpdate call.

docs.title: delete_row(row_number_or_instance, *, shift_up=True)
docs.text: Delete a row by number or bound instance. When shift_up=True (default) subsequent rows shift up (Google Sheets native behaviour); the cache is updated accordingly.

docs.title: Other Methods
docs.text:
• clear_cache() — discard the in-memory row cache.
  • apply_formats_for_model() — apply GSFormat annotations as column-level number formats.
  • get_last_row_number() — best-effort detection of the last populated row.

docs.title: Date and Datetime Helpers
docs.text:
from pydantic_gsheets import gsheets_to_datetime, gsheets_to_date, datetime_to_gsheets
  • gsheets_to_datetime(serial) → datetime (UTC-aware, preserves time)
  • gsheets_to_date(serial) → date (time component dropped)
  • datetime_to_gsheets(d) → float serial number

Fields typed as datetime use gsheets_to_datetime; fields typed as date use gsheets_to_date. The type annotation is the source of truth.

docs.title: Retry & Rate Limiting
docs.text:
All API calls go through SheetsClient which applies:

  • Token-bucket rate limiter — 290 req/min (Google's quota is 300/min).
  • Exponential backoff — retries on 429 / 5xx with jitter.

Tune via RetryConfig:

from pydantic_gsheets import SheetsClient, RetryConfig

client = SheetsClient(service, retry_config=RetryConfig(max_attempts=3))
